identity.title: Sharpness and Locality for Percolation on Finite Transitive Graphs

assessment: Major revision required: the core finite-graph cost lemmas are false after volume saturation; eight local issues admit bounded corrections.
outcome: One confirmed Major and eight confirmed Minor findings. Exact-source initial scientific review complete; independent scientific acceptance pending.

problems.title: Finite-volume saturation invalidates the central cost lemmas
locations: p20 definition of Delta and Lemma 3.5
problems.claim: The finite-graph cost becomes arbitrarily small on a suitable orange interval and is at most 1/log log n when L(n) is green.
problems.hypotheses_checked: C3 is finite connected vertex-transitive of degree2; t=0 gives p=1/2 and all-pair connectivity5/8. Epsilon1/2 and n1=exp24 meet t<=1/epsilon. Every larger n is low-growth and orange. For Lemma3.5 n=exp(exp k), k>=48 arbitrarily large, has L(n)=exp(k/2) green.
problems.decisive_evidence: Empty outer spheres force U_s(n)=floor(n^(1/3)/8), growth3, so Delta=(log log n/log3)^(1/4) tends to infinity at every time. On n>=exp24 it is >1, and at n=exp(exp k) it exceeds1>1/k.
problems.impact: False central auxiliary assertions used by Lemma3.2 and Proposition3.1. Theorem1.1 itself is not refuted by a fixed triangle.
problems.repair: Set cost to0 when floor(n^(1/3))>diamG, retaining the original cost otherwise; orange already implies green there. Finite-limit costs then vanish, while fixed-scale infinite local limits are unchanged. Propagate the altered definition and address P7 explicitly.
problems.repair_limits: Checks the saturated branch and its compactness interface; not an assertion of whole-paper acceptance or author adoption.
problems.evidence_kind: All-hypothesis analytic counterexamples plus exact triangle enumeration

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Finite-graph setup p.18, green/tube definition p.19, cost and Lemma3.5 p.20, Lemma3.6 p.21, finite-limit argument p.24, appendix pp.42-43. No diameter upper bound on the scale is imposed.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: C3 is simple connected finite transitive degree2. At t=0,phi=1/2, all-pair connection minimum5/8, independently enumerated. For epsilon1/2,n1=exp24, every n>=n1 is low-growth and orange. Empty outer spheres make U_s(n)=floor(n^(1/3)/8), with growth3 at all times.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Delta_s(n)=(log log n/log3)^(1/4)>1 for n>=exp24, so no interval in Lemma3.6 can meet its bound. For arbitrary k>=48, n=exp(exp k), L(n)=exp(k/2) is green because every tube covers C3 and delta(R(L))<1/2. Yet Delta0(n)=(k/log3)^(1/4)>1>1/k, refuting Lemma3.5 at arbitrarily large scales.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The fixed triangle is not an infinite family and does not refute Theorem1.1. A local limit that is finite is eventually the same connected regular graph once a sufficiently large ball matches.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Lemmas3.5/3.6 feed3.2 then Proposition3.1 and Claim6.1. Actual false core auxiliary assertions justify Major even without a main-theorem counterexample.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Set Delta*=0 when floor(n^(1/3))>diamG. In that branch Bn and every n-tube are G, so orange implies green without sprinkling. Finite-limit costs become eventually zero; infinite local limits at any fixed scale are unchanged. This verifies the identified branch, not all imported estimates or the whole induction; definitions and P7 must be updated consistently.

problems.title: Closed-ball overlap invalidates a deterministic packing implication
problems.hypotheses_checked: G=C_L Cartesian K10,10, L even large, p=delta=.9,r1,n55; degree12, ball13; choose L for any positive c. W is a full bipartition maximal2-separated and a valid H-spanning tree contains the ten-vertex fibre star.
problems.decisive_evidence: Open only the100 edges of one K10,10 fibre. All10 events A_u hold with local intersection11>=117/20, but root cluster20<55. Configuration probability is strictly positive. Explicit L600 graph computed with12000 vertices72000 edges.
problems.impact: The proof implication fails; the final lemma inequality is not disproved.
problems.repair: Use a maximal net with separation>2 floor(r). Closed balls are disjoint; 2R-cover and H-edges<=5R preserve the volume/Harris argument.
problems.repair_limits: A local packing correction; no assertion that the original overlapping count is valid.
problems.evidence_kind: Positive-probability all-hypothesis configuration and graph computation

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Lemma2.7 proof p.13 sums sizes of closed balls from centers separated by >=2r.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: C_L Cartesian K10,10 is finite connected transitive degree12 for large even L. At p=delta=.9,r1,n55, ball size13 and neighbor connections >=delta. Choose L to meet n<=c|V|/13 for any proposed c>0. A full bipartition is maximal2-separated; the ten first-side vertices in one fiber support an H-tree star.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Open just the100 fiber edges, a positive-probability configuration. All ten Au occur: parent connections hold and local counts11>=117/20. Their cluster has20<55 vertices, while ceil(110/11.7)=10. The deterministic implication is false.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This does not refute the final probability bound. A maximal net of mutual distance>2 floor(r) has disjoint closed balls and a2R cover; its H is connected with edge lengths<=4R+1<=5R.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Local packing/counting step with a concrete repair; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use the strict integer net; the five-link Harris and volume arguments retain qualitative constants.

problems.title: Variance bound needs an integer threshold or ceiling
problems.hypotheses_checked: C3, p=1/100, real threshold n=6/5 falls within the printed unrestricted n>=0; application later uses a generally real threshold.
problems.decisive_evidence: Exact eight-configuration enumeration gives E=597/10000 and Var=11672991/10^8, greater than n^2 E=21492/250000. Stopped exploration has ceil(n) vertices.
problems.impact: Literal real-threshold claim false; integer-threshold proof remains available.
problems.repair: State n integer or replace n^2 by ceil(n)^2 and round the application, absorbing the bounded error.
problems.repair_limits: If integers were intended implicitly this is a required domain clarification, not a failure of the integer theorem.
problems.evidence_kind: Exact rational enumeration and exploration bound

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Lemma2.8 p.14 says all n>=0; p.15 uses generally real c|Br|log|V|.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: C3,p1/100,n6/5 makes X the nonisolated vertices. All eight configurations have been enumerated exactly.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: E=597/10000, Var=11672991/10^8, whereas n^2 E=5373/62500. The stopped exploration can have ceil(n), not n, vertices.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: For integer thresholds the argument is not refuted. If an implicit integer convention was intended, the explicit real application still needs rounding.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use ceil(n)^2 or an integer threshold and absorb bounded rounding in the asymptotic application.

problems.title: Corollary2.3 is invoked with lambda below1
problems.hypotheses_checked: The corollary explicitly requires lambda>=1, while lambda=n/log|V| is used for every n>=1.
problems.decisive_evidence: All1<=n<log|V| violate the cited hypothesis, with an unbounded excluded range as |V| grows.
problems.impact: The written all-n exponential-tail inference has a domain gap.
problems.repair: Apply Lemma2.2 directly with h=r^-1 log(1/(1-epsilon/4)), yielding mu<=epsilon/2 and a uniform exponential bound for every n>=1.
problems.repair_limits: Uses the finite ghost-field proof verified from the retained Vanneuville primary article; conclusion not refuted.
problems.evidence_kind: Hypothesis mismatch and complete replacement inequality

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Corollary2.3 p.11 requires lambda>=1; Proposition2.9 pp.15-16 substitutes n/log|V| for every n>=1.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: The excluded interval1<=n<log|V| is unbounded as the graph grows. The chosen finite r and p0=(1-epsilon/2)pc(H) give tail at r <=epsilon/4.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Direct ghost comparison with h=log(1/(1-epsilon/4))/r gives mu<=epsilon/2 and tail at (1-epsilon/2)p0 <=(1-epsilon/2)^-1 exp(-hn) for every n. Since (1-epsilon/2)^2>=1-epsilon, monotonicity gives the desired target bound.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The retained2025 reference's finite exploration lemma applies to the entire finite graph: conditional unseen-edge law remains product, transitivity bounds the pivotal ghost event, and Bayes gives the displayed comparison without an infinite-volume limit.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Invalid cited-lemma domain, with full local replacement inequality. Minor; proposition not refuted.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use Lemma2.2 directly and a uniform constant.

problems.title: The chosen radius does not control the displayed error
problems.hypotheses_checked: Positive C, degree d>=2 and delta>0; the algebra applies exactly to the printed radius. Numerical example is an algebraic test, not an asserted graph in the contradiction case.
problems.decisive_evidence: Substitution yields r delta^2/(2d), exceeding delta^2/2 once r>d. d4,C1,delta1/2,n2^46 gives r8,error1/4,target1/8.
problems.impact: The claimed lower bound does not follow from that radius choice.
problems.repair: Use half the logarithmic radius, rounded down, and r<=d^r; then error<=delta^2/(2d). New radius still diverges.
problems.evidence_kind: Symbolic substitution with exact rational independent check

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Case2 error Cr d^(r+1)/sqrt(n), p.16, and selected logarithmic radius p.17.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: The algebra is under the printed positive constants; the numerical witness is not asserted to be a graph in the contradiction case.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Substitution gives r delta^2/(2d), not <=delta^2/2 for arbitrary large n. Exact d4,C1,delta1/2,n2^46 yields r8,error1/4,target1/8.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Half the logarithmic radius, rounded down, still diverges and using r<=d^r bounds the error by delta^2/(2d).
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Local radius algebra, Minor; conclusion not refuted.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use the smaller radius and retain the large-n range.

problems.title: Unrestricted eta makes a probability lower bound exceed1
problems.hypotheses_checked: Eta5, any proposed c(2,5)>0; lambda=exp(1/c+1/c^2), large cycle C_N and p=1-N^-2 satisfy the premise by the all-open event.
problems.decisive_evidence: The conclusion requires at least25/20 while all connection probabilities are at most1. N can be chosen to meet lambda logN<=N and1/(cN^c)<=1/2.
problems.impact: The printed parameter-unrestricted proposition is false; intended small-sprinkling application is unaffected after correction.
problems.repair: Restrict eta to the proved small range or cap the asserted bound by a fixed small-sprinkling value.
problems.repair_limits: An unqualified 'may assume eta<=1/2' does not prove the printed eta^2 dependence for larger eta.
problems.evidence_kind: All-hypothesis family and elementary union bound

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Proposition2.1 p.11 allows all eta>0 and conclusion eta^2/20; proof p.12 reduces to eta<=1/2 without preserving that RHS.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For eta5 and any c(2,5)>0 choose lambda=exp(1/c+1/c^2), giving ball radius1. Choose large C_N with lambda logN<=N,1/(cN^c)<=1/2, and p=1-N^-2.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: All-open event probability>=1-1/N>=1/2 supplies the premise. Clamped p+eta=1 still cannot give a probability>=25/20.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The small-sprinkling range actually used admits the stated proof after restriction.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False extra parameter range with bounded correction; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: State the small eta range or cap the bound by a proven fixed-small-sprinkling value.

problems.title: The gamma expression is not real on permitted cycles
problems.hypotheses_checked: Even cycles C_2m are finite transitive and have diameter m; their diameter-normalized vertex metric embeds isometrically in the intrinsic unit circle.
problems.decisive_evidence: The embedding gives0<gamma<=pi/2<e. Consequently log log gamma^+ is undefined when gamma<=1 and negative when1<gamma<e; the square root is not a real bound.
problems.impact: The proposition requires a small-gamma case or domain restriction. Section6 has gamma diverging and so eventually avoids this defect.
problems.repair: State an adequate large-gamma domain including the starting scale, or prove a separate small-gamma conclusion. Also reduce epsilon below1/2 before choosing positive alpha.
problems.repair_limits: Merely flooring gamma at3 does not prove the modified quantitative claim.
problems.evidence_kind: Exact metric embedding and domain calculation

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Gamma and gamma+ in Proposition3.1 pp.17-18, coloring only at n>=3 and positive-alpha choice p.18.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Even C2m embeds isometrically after diameter normalization into the intrinsic unit circle. Hausdorff gap<=pi/(2m) and diam=m give0<gamma<=pi/2<e.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: For gamma<=1, log log gamma+ is undefined; for1<gamma<e it is negative. The real square-root bound is not defined. Phi(1/alpha)=1-epsilon with alpha>0 additionally requires epsilon<1/2.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The actual Section6 use has gamma>exp((log diam)^(1/9)), eventually large. Merely flooring gamma at3 is not a proof of a new bound.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Quantitative statement domain defect, bounded in the main application. Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Explicit large-gamma and small-epsilon reductions, or a separately proved small-gamma conclusion.

problems.title: Uniformly bounded individual cycles cannot approximate a bi-infinite geodesic
problems.hypotheses_checked: Z2 is one-ended with cycle-space generator diameter2.
problems.decisive_evidence: Two sufficiently separated edges of the horizontal axis would eventually both lie in each approximating cycle, contradicting diameter<=2.
problems.impact: The stated explanatory equivalence is false; the actual finite cycle-space proof of Lemma3.17 does not rely on it.
problems.repair: Use finite sums of bounded generators. Growing rectangle boundaries provide the correct pointwise approximation in Z2.
problems.repair_limits: Does not claim that arbitrary graphs have the corrected one-ended equivalence without its proper hypotheses.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Cycles paragraph p.28 expressly says individual cycles of diameter<=delta(G); actual Lemma3.17 proof p.45 uses finite sums.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Z2 is one-ended, unit plaquettes generate its finite cycle space, delta=2.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Pointwise convergence to the horizontal bi-infinite axis would eventually include two arbitrarily separated axis edges in a single diameter2 cycle, impossible.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Growing rectangle boundaries converge pointwise to the axis and are finite sums of unit plaquettes, but have unbounded diameter. The p.45 cutset argument uses this finite-sum type of algebra, not the false sentence.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Incorrect explanatory equivalence with no demonstrated core dependency; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Replace with an appropriately qualified finite-sums statement or omit; no general corrected equivalence certified.

problems.title: Density quantiles do not exist for certain events
problems.decisive_evidence: Largest cluster density is always at least1/3, so event probability1 for every p and never1/2.
problems.impact: The equality definition and zero-denominator quotient need endpoint conventions; the large-volume usage is away from this range.
problems.repair: Use generalized infimum quantiles in[0,1] and multiplicative sharp-density inequality, or restrict alpha>1/|V|.
problems.repair_limits: No counterexample to Proposition4.1 in its actual asymptotic use.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Equality quantile and sharp-density quotient p.33; retained EH v2 Definition3.1 p.17 gives an infimum convention.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: C3,alpha1/4,delta1/2 lie in the displayed open ranges.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Largest cluster density is always>=1/3, so its threshold event has probability1 for every p and can never equal1/2.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Generalized infimum gives zero; the ratio0/0 must also be addressed. Large-volume proof uses densities above the microscopic regime.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Endpoint/definition correction, Minor; no Proposition4.1 counterexample.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use infimum in[0,1] and multiplicative inequality, or restrict alpha>1/|V|.

limitations: The explicit triangle witnesses refute Lemmas3.5 and3.6, not the infinite-family Theorem1.1.
The piecewise zero-cost repair was checked in the saturated branch and compactness interface; no whole-paper acceptance or author adoption is asserted.
The packing configuration refutes the printed deterministic proof implication, not the final probability inequality of Lemma2.7.
The variance counterexample concerns real thresholds; the integer-threshold argument is not refuted.
The radius example is an exact algebraic calculation, not an asserted graph satisfying the contradiction case of Proposition2.9.
The gamma domain requires an explicit separate treatment; flooring gamma at3 is not claimed sufficient.
The exact arXivv1 was reviewed; journal-version equivalence is not asserted.
Relevant complete units in three primary arXiv references and all12pages of a fourth published primary article were read. This is not a recursive review of all cited literature.
No author code executed; code absence is not a mathematical defect.
UI identity is controller-observed; runtime GPT-6 Astra Pro. Backend equivalence not independently verified.
